absent: Physical to virtual interrupt mapping lifecycle beyond initial mapping, including unmapping and teardown sequencing.
Detailed layout of arch timer per CPU and per context structures and timer data fields beyond referenced members.
Interrupt controller initialization sequencing and distributor state machine that gates ownership claims.
Hypervisor page table walker internals and protection attribute translation rules.
Counter offset application to running virtual CPUs and interaction with live migration restore path.
Device attribute ABI identifiers and user structure layouts beyond symbolic names.
Nested virtualization initialization and teardown behavior referenced during virtual machine creation.
Translation fault handling and memory slot integration beyond empty checks.

findings.text: Host timer subsystem startup validates that arch timer information and its timecounter are present, normalizes virtual and physical interrupt configuration, registers per CPU handlers for guest timer interrupts, and when a kernel interrupt controller is present binds affinity and enables the active state optimization, cleaning up previously acquired interrupts on failure.

Virtual timer interrupt must be a positive identifier and trigger type is constrained to level high or level low, with any other firmware described type rejected in favour of level low accompanied by an error report.

Timer private interrupts must be distinct across the timer population for a virtual CPU and become immutable after successful validation, with GICv5 additionally requiring each entry to match its default private value.

Virtual machine architecture configuration lock serializes assignment and validation of timer private interrupts and guards user updates to timer interrupt routing against concurrent validation that would freeze the routing.

Timer enablement is idempotent and proceeds from disabled to enabled, bypassing virtual to physical mapping when no kernel interrupt controller exists and otherwise requiring successful interrupt validation and ops selection followed by mapping of direct virtual and optional direct physical timers before marking the per CPU state enabled.

Timer input level query operates on the currently running virtual CPU, scans its timer contexts for a context whose virtual interrupt matches the queried identifier and reports pending state, warning when no context matches.

Interrupt ownership can be claimed only after interrupt controller initialization and only for private or valid shared identifiers, with conflicting claims by a different owner rejected and repeated claims by the same owner accepted.
Per interrupt spin lock with interrupt save protects ownership assignment and operations pointer replacement against concurrent distributor and timer paths.

Timer control exposes user operations to assign, query and probe timer interrupt routing for virtual, physical and hypervisor timer views, plus a virtual machine operation to install a shared virtual and physical counter offset.

User timer routing updates require a kernel interrupt controller and a private interrupt value, are rejected as busy once routing has been frozen, defer uniqueness checking until initial run, while counter offset updates require reserved field to be clear, reject protected guests, and require exclusive access to all virtual CPUs.
Capability mapping table pairs a virtual machine control identifier with an extension capability code, allowing lookup of the required extension for a given control.

Basic ARM capability is defined to alias the virtual CPU count capability, and virtual machine controls for interrupt controller creation, device address, tag copy, device attribute access, counter offset, register mask ranges and preferred target each map to their documented extension capabilities.
Capability lookup scans the static mapping table for a matching control and returns its extension through an out parameter, signalling invalid argument when no entry matches.

Virtual machine creation validates type mask, initializes configuration lock, shares the virtual machine structure with the hypervisor, allocates supported CPU mask, initializes translation and nested state, initializes protected state or rejects protected type when protection is unavailable, then performs early interrupt controller and timer initialization, sets maximum virtual CPU count, initializes hypercalls and clears feature bitmap, unwinding prior steps on failure.

Enable capability handling rejects any set flags and disallowed protected extensions, and each capability carries its own precondition such as absence of created virtual CPUs for memory tagging and writable implementation defined registers, empty memory slots for eager split sizing with supported block size, and absence of guest memory for tagging.
Hypercall initialization installs standard, standard hypervisor and vendor hypervisor feature bitmaps and initializes the configuration filter structure for the virtual machine.

Hypervisor sharing is a no operation when already in hypervisor mode, rejects virtual or module addresses, creates direct mappings when the host owns hypervisor mappings, and otherwise shares each page in the range through reference counted hypercalls with rollback of already shared pages on failure.
Shared page tree mutex serializes lookup, insertion, reference count adjustment and removal of shared page descriptors, while hypervisor page table mutex serializes creation of hypervisor mappings.
Host owns hypervisor mappings only when not in hypervisor mode and protection has not been finalized, with early protected boot without a page table treated as unowned.

Hypervisor mapping creation validates host ownership, aligns the virtual range to page boundaries and maps each page with requested protections, delegating individual range mapping to a page table walk that translates protections, walks leaf entries and orders with barriers.

Broken offset hardware workaround is enabled only when sanitized feature registers report virtualization host extensions without the companion extension variant together with enhanced counter virtualization plus host extension active and a specific hardware workaround capability, causing virtual timer accesses to trap.

Failed unshare during rollback leaks the page as permanently shared with the hypervisor without breaking isolation, conflicting interrupt ownership fails with existence error, use before interrupt controller initialization fails with retryable error, and missing physical timer on virtualization host extensions fails startup with device error.

Wait for interrupt and wait for event trap policies default to task scoped no trap with alternatives for unconditional no trap and unconditional trap, and virtual CPU kick is required only when the virtual CPU is observed exiting guest mode inside guest mode.
Per CPU hypervisor stack base and initialization flag provide per processor hypervisor state, while global flags record interrupt controller presence and overall ARM virtualization initialization.

Virtualization host extension timer initialization enables enhanced counter virtualization in the hypervisor timer control when the corresponding capability is present, and virtual CPU termination cancels its background software timer.
Timer user ABI distinguishes virtual, physical and hypervisor timer interrupt selectors for set, get and probe operations.
